newsitem.title: USA: Continental DC-9 makes emergency landing in Houston.
newsitem.headline: Continental DC-9 makes emergency landing in Houston.

text.p: A Continental Airlines DC-9 with 101 passengers and crew on board was forced to make an emergency landing in Houston on Tuesday after the pilot reported a possible fire in one of the engines, officials said.

Flames could be seen coming from the right engine of the airplane by controllers in the tower as Flight 1682 returned to Houston Intercontinental Airport about 20 minutes after taking off for Indianapolis, they said.
"They had some kind of problem on the number two engine, the right engine. It was either red hot or there were flames coming from it," said Richard Fernandez of the Texas Department of Aviation.
A Continental spokesman said the pilot noticed an indicator light signaling a problem with the engine shortly after taking off and requested the emergency landing.

"The indication was that there was some smoke coming from the engine. At this point we don't know if there was actually a fire or if there was an excess fuel burn," Continental spokesman Ned Walker said.
The emergency occured as a strong thunderstorm moved into the area. There were no injuries and passengers used emergency stairs to evacuate the airplane and were taken back to the terminal on buses.
"It was a little exciting ride, but nothing too dangerous," Fernandez said.
